text:
ravi: Heads-up — planning a phased Terraform cutover for inter-region VPC peering + IAM role update. Target change window tomorrow 03/08 01:00-02:00 UTC. Goal: minimal disruption; we'll apply peering first in us-east-1, validate, then roll eu-west-1, then ap-southeast-1.

maya: ack. can you list the exact tf modules + provider pins? also want the deploybot slots so we can coordinate oncall. :eyes:

ravi: yes. plan below. provider pin to hashicorp/aws v4.3.0 in root module (we're avoiding the 4.5 behavior). primary apply: module.vpc_peering, module.route_tables, module.iam_roles (iam change is additive but needs careful principal update). terraform commands:```
terraform init -upgrade=false
terraform plan -target=module.vpc_peering -var-file=prod.vars.tfvars
terraform apply -target=module.vpc_peering -parallelism=10 -auto-approve
```
we'll run module.iam_roles after peering verifies.

deploybot: deploybot: apply request queued. Slot assigned: slot-3 (window 01:00-01:20 UTC). Preflight checks: state lock available, remote state healthy, no concurrent applies. Preflight output: OK.

sam: Quick Q on rollback criteria — what triggers immediate rollback vs pause + fix? I suggest: immediate rollback if VPC peering fails to establish OR if cross-region service 5xx increases > 5% for 10m after rollout edge. Otherwise pause and investigate.

lee: +1 to sam. Also add health checks: run curl to internal /_hc endpoint across AZs and traceroutes for critical flows. If BGP/route propagation delays, we should be ready to revert route changes.

oncall-ops: noted. I'll be oncall for the window and will run connectivity validations. My playbook excerpt:```
# after apply completes
aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=status-code,Values=active
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc>
# sanity test from a bastion in each region
curl -sS http://internal-service/_hc | jq .status
traceroute -n <service-ip>
```
if any step fails, I will post `ROLLBACK` in this thread and execute:```
terraform apply -target=module.vpc_peering -refresh=false -var-file=prod.vars.tfvars
# if needed, restore state from snapshot: terraform state pull > state.json && restore via state push (per runbook)
```

ravi: good. decision policy: roll forward unless either peering create fails or 5xx spike >5% sustained for 10m. If we see config drift or provider error (eg provider v4.x unexpected), escalate and consider pin rollback to previous tfstate snapshot.

maya: can you add short release note blurb for infra changelog? I'll forward to release-managers. Suggested: "Add inter-region VPC peering and principle update to iam roles; phased rollout across regions, provider pinned to aws v4.3.0. Change window 03/08 01:00-02:00 UTC. Contact @oncall-ops for post-apply checks."

ravi: done, pushed to docs/release-notes/infra.md and attached the apply plan output to the deploy ticket.

deploybot: deploybot: preflight finished, schedule confirmed. Will post status updates: PREPARED -> RUNNING -> COMPLETED/FAILED. Auto-lock TTL: 30m.

oncall-ops: I'll start a monitoring snapshot 15m prior and a traffic baseline. ping here when baseline ready.

sam: leaving a note — if we need immediate traffic fallbacks, route table can be adjusted to steer traffic to legacy peering tunnel (runbook entry 4.2). Confirmed with networking.

ravi: thanks everyone. final checklist: pin provider 4.3.0, backup state snapshot, notify release-managers, oncall ready, deploybot slot confirmed. meet in thread 45m before window to go over last-minute flags. :thumbsup:

lee: prepping scripts for post-apply validation and will share results in thread.

deploybot: deploybot: running slot check 1778256000 -> slot-3 reserved. No conflicting applies.

oncall-ops: baseline ready. starting 15m countdown.

ravi: see you all in the window. if anyone can't make it, post here and assign a backup.
